title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #794 (1969, DISPROVED): Is it true that every 3-uniform hypergraph on 3n vertices with at least n³+1 edges must contain K₄⁻ (4 vertices, 3 edges) or a 5-7 configuration? Balogh showed the 5-7 condition is redundant. Harris provided a counterexample: 9 vertices, 28 edges, no K₄⁻. The correct Turán density for K₄⁻ is at least 2/7 (Frankl-Füredi 1984), making the n³+1 threshold (density 2/9) insufficient.
mathContext: A 3-uniform hypergraph $H = (V, E)$ has $E \subseteq \binom{V}{3}$. The Turán density $\pi(F)$ for a forbidden 3-graph $F$ is $\lim_{n \to \infty} \max\{|E|/\binom{n}{3} : |V| = n, F \not\subseteq H\}$. For $K_4^- = $ (4 vertices, 3 edges), the density $n^3 + 1$ on $3n$ vertices corresponds to density $\frac{n^3}{\binom{3n}{3}} \approx \frac{n^3}{(3n)^3/6} = \frac{2}{9}$, which is below the Frankl-Füredi lower bound $\pi(K_4^-) \geq 2/7 \approx 0.286$.

title: Hypergraph3 Structure
content: Hypergraph3 V is a structure with vertices (Finset V), edges (Finset (Finset V)), and proofs that every edge has exactly 3 elements and is a subset of vertices. vertexCount and edgeCount extract cardinalities.
mathContext: The structure encodes a 3-uniform hypergraph $H = (V, E)$ where $E \subseteq \binom{V}{3}$. The field $\texttt{edge\_card}$ ensures 3-uniformity: $\forall e \in E,\; |e| = 3$. The field $\texttt{edge\_subset}$ ensures $e \subseteq V$. Using $\texttt{Finset (Finset V)}$ for edges means edges are unordered sets, matching the hypergraph convention. The maximum possible edge count is $\binom{|V|}{3}$.

title: ContainsK4Minus and Contains5_7
content: ContainsK4Minus H means ∃ S with |S| = 4, S ⊆ V, and exactly 3 edges within S. Contains5_7 H means ∃ S with |S| = 5 and exactly 7 edges within S. In a 3-uniform hypergraph, K₄⁻ has 4 vertices with 3 of the possible 4 edges — one edge 'missing.'
mathContext: For 4 vertices in a 3-uniform hypergraph, there are $\binom{4}{3} = 4$ possible edges. $K_4^-$ uses 3 of these 4 edges. For 5 vertices, $\binom{5}{3} = 10$ possible edges; 7 edges is a high-density subhypergraph. The filter $\texttt{H.edges.filter}(e \subseteq S)$ counts edges within the vertex subset $S$. Note that the 5-7 configuration is dense enough ($7/10 = 0.7$) that it must contain $K_4^-$ as a sub-configuration — this is Balogh's observation.

title: Balogh's Observation
content: balogh_observation axiomatizes: Contains5_7 H → ContainsK4Minus H. Any 5-vertex set with 7 of 10 possible edges contains a 4-vertex subset with 3 of 4 possible edges. second_condition_redundant simply applies this axiom. This simplifies the problem to asking only about K₄⁻.
mathContext: The proof is a counting argument: among 5 vertices, each 4-vertex subset has $\binom{5}{4} = 5$ possible selections. With 7 edges on 5 vertices (out of 10 possible), each 4-vertex subset inherits at least $7 - \binom{4}{3} = 7 - 4 = 3$ edges on average by inclusion-exclusion. More precisely, each edge is counted by $\binom{5-3}{1} = 2$ of the 5 subsets, so the total edges across all subsets is $7 \times 2 = 14$, averaging $14/5 = 2.8$ per subset. At least one subset has $\geq 3$ edges, giving $K_4^-$.

title: Original and Simplified Conjectures
content: Erdos794Conjecture: ∀ H on 3n vertices with ≥ n³+1 edges, ContainsK4Minus H ∨ Contains5_7 H. Erdos794Simplified: the same with just ContainsK4Minus. simplified_implies_original (PROVED): the simplified version implies the original by taking the left disjunct.
mathContext: The original conjecture $\forall H,\; |V| = 3n \wedge |E| \geq n^3 + 1 \implies K_4^- \subseteq H \vee \texttt{5-7} \subseteq H$ is weakened to the simplified version $\forall H,\; |V| = 3n \wedge |E| \geq n^3 + 1 \implies K_4^- \subseteq H$. The implication $\texttt{Simplified} \implies \texttt{Original}$ is trivial (left injection into disjunction). The converse uses Balogh: $\texttt{Original} \implies \texttt{Simplified}$ because $\texttt{5-7} \implies K_4^-$. So the two are equivalent, and disproving either disproves both.

title: Harris's Counterexample
content: HarrisCounterexample structure for n=3: 9 vertices (Fin 9), 28 edges, all 3-element. The construction: 27 cross-product edges {a,b,c} with a ∈ {1,2,3}, b ∈ {4,5,6}, c ∈ {7,8,9}, plus edge {1,2,3}. n3_threshold (PROVED): 3³+1 = 28. harris_counterexample_exists axiom: ∃ H on Fin 9 with 9 vertices, 28 edges, ¬ContainsK4Minus.
mathContext: The construction is a tripartite product: partition $\{1,\ldots,9\}$ into $A = \{1,2,3\}$, $B = \{4,5,6\}$, $C = \{7,8,9\}$, and take all $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ cross-product triples $\{a, b, c\}$ with $a \in A, b \in B, c \in C$. This is a balanced tripartite 3-graph. Adding the single intra-partition edge $\{1,2,3\}$ gives 28 edges total. **Why no $K_4^-$?** Any 4 vertices with 3 edges would need 3 triples sharing at least 2 vertices in some pair of parts, but the cross-product structure prevents this: each pair of parts contributes at most one element per edge, so 4 vertices span at most 2 cross-product edges. The additional edge $\{1,2,3\}$ is within $A$, so it can't combine with cross-product edges to form $K_4^-$.

title: Turán Density and Frankl-Füredi Bound
content: turanDensityK4Minus is defined as the real number 2/7 (conjectured value). frankl_furedi_lower axiomatizes that this density is ≥ 2/7. turan_conjecture records Turán's earlier conjecture of 1/4. current_conjecture states the believed value 2/7.
mathContext: The Turán density $\pi(K_4^-)$ is defined as $\lim_{n \to \infty} \max\{|E|/\binom{n}{3} : H \text{ is } K_4^-\text{-free on } n \text{ vertices}\}$. Frankl and Füredi (1984) proved $\pi(K_4^-) \geq 2/7$ by constructing a $K_4^-$-free 3-graph achieving this density: the 'Fano complement' construction. Turán conjectured $\pi(K_4^-) = 1/4$ (based on the complete balanced tripartite 3-graph), but $2/7 > 1/4 = 0.25$, disproving Turán's conjecture for this specific forbidden hypergraph. The current belief $\pi(K_4^-) = 2/7$ remains open — proving the matching upper bound is a major challenge in extremal hypergraph theory.
